grades.reason: Exercises on messaging and RPC middleware. They have nothing to do with RISC-V FMV.X.W or FCVT.W.S.

grades.quote: The bits are not modified in the transfer, and in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.
grades.reason: Describes the FMV.X.W side of the comparison: a raw bit-pattern move from the FP register to the integer register, with no modification and NaN payloads preserved. It does not describe FCVT.W.S, so the contrast with numeric conversion is only implicit.

A register and CSR listing. FCVT.W.S depends on frm and accumulates NV and NX flags, while FMV.X.W has no rounding mode and no accumulating flags. This hints at a difference but does not explain the bit-move versus numeric-conversion distinction.
Covers the Q-extension quad-precision conversions (FCVT.W.Q and similar) and sign injection. It mentions neither FMV.X.W nor FCVT.W.S, so it doesn't answer the question.
